summary: Automated environment-permission-reconcile job briefly revoked data-platform service account access for prod-us-east
description:
Issue summary: During a scheduled run of the automated environment-permission-reconciliation job (reconcile-runner), multiple data-platform service accounts used by the data ingestion pipelines lost access to a subset of production resources in prod-us-east. The job applied an org-policy alignment change that removed a tag used upstream by the private-deploy onboarding flow, causing short-lived permission denials.

Why this ticket: capture investigation, temporary rollback actions, and next steps to prevent recurrence.
impact: Data ingestion pipelines experienced transient failures (~35 minutes) across three nightly runs. No customer-facing API was affected, but internal analytics and downstream model retraining jobs were delayed. Estimated job-run backlog ~ 12 hours for affected pipelines. Two on-call pager escalations were triggered.
environment_details: Prod account master/org structure: GCP org: redwood-prod (projects: prod-us-east-data, prod-us-east-llm). Reconcile-runner runs as a cross-account IAM service principal (aws-assumer:reconcile-runner, gcp-sa:reconcile-runner@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com). Reconcile job implements org-policy normalization and tag-to-role syncs.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Trigger reconcile-runner with tag-normalize=true against prod-us-east dry-run=false. 2) Job evaluates projects under org and translates policy tags to ephemeral role bindings. 3) If tag key 'env:deployment' absent, job removes fallback binding 'data-platform-reader:fallback' and leaves only tag-scoped bindings. 4) Data-platform service accounts without the tag lose effective access.
logs_and_signals:
- reconcile-runner logs (2026-03-12T01:12:03Z): applied binding removal on projects/prod-us-east-data: removed IAM binding data-platform-reader:fallback
- Stackdriver (prod-us-east-data) authz logs: repeated 403s from service-account data-platform-pipeline-sa@prod-us-east-data.iam.gserviceaccount.com starting 2026-03-12T01:15Z
- Pager duty notes: #oncall notified at 2026-03-12T01:23Z
- reconcile-runner metrics: job-duration 182s, affected-projects 3, failed-bindings 0
- Audit logs show subsequent reconcile rollback at 2026-03-12T01:50Z triggered by infra-ops alerting rule 'reconcile-unexpected-binding-changes'
initial_investigation_notes:
- Hypothesis 1: A recent reconcile-runner change (PR 412) tightened role-scoping to prefer tag-scoped bindings and removed a default fallback. The change was merged last week and scheduled for daily runs.
- Hypothesis 2: Org-policy enforcement for tag presence was recently enabled for a subset of GCP folders; reconcile-runner removed bindings where tag was absent.
- Evidence: PR 412 includes code that drops fallback bindings when tag key missing (see PR diff). The audit trail shows the binding removal correlates with job start times.
- Quick repro in staging: ran reconcile-runner against staging-project with tag removed; observed identical binding removal behavior.
temporary_mitigation: 1) Rolled back reconcile-runner to previous stable image (tag v2026-03-05) at 2026-03-12T01:52Z. 2) Re-applied fallback IAM binding 'data-platform-reader:fallback' to prod projects affected. 3) Requeued stalled ingestion jobs; pipelines resumed by 2026-03-12T02:05Z. 4) Created an alert on 'binding-removal-without-tag' to stop future runs until patching done.
root_cause_hypothesis: Change in reconcile-runner (PR 412) removed the 'safe-fallback' binding if tag absent. When combined with a recently enforced org-policy that strips the 'env:deployment' tag for some onboarding projects, the reconciliation job interpreted lack of tag as signal to remove fallback bindings, resulting in access loss.
fix_and_next_steps:
Short term: pin reconcile-runner to v2026-03-05 for prod runs and keep alerting in place. Medium term: update reconcile-runner to preserve fallback bindings and add a dry-run gating for first-run in newly onboarded projects. Long term: implement pre-flight checks that detect tag absence and notify owners instead of removing bindings.
Owners: Marco Ruiz (infra) to land code fix; Aisha Khan to coordinate with Data Platform to validate bindings; Security (Leah Park) to review org-policy rollout plan.
Planned PRs: github.com/redwood-inference/reconcile-runner/pull/418 (preserve-fallback), PR 419 (preflight-checks).
resolution: Workaround and rollback applied; reconcile-runner pinned and fallback bindings re-applied. Code patch PR #418 opened to preserve fallback binding behavior and add explicit opt-in gating for tag normalization. Monitoring: additional alert added and a runbook updated. Incident not escalated to customers.
follow_up_actions: 1) Postmortem write-up due 2026-03-20 (owner: Marco Ruiz). 2) Update runbook 'Env Reconcile Runbook' with preflight checklist and safe-rollback steps (owner: SRE). 3) Security to review org-policy rollout checklist and coordinate with onboarding team. 4) Add unit/integration tests in reconcile-runner to cover fallback binding cases.
comments: Aisha Khan (reporter): Initial triage notes and rollback coordinated with infra at 01:50Z. Marking P1 due to multiple pipeline failures.
Marco Ruiz (assignee): Rolled back to v2026-03-05; re-applied bindings; opening patch PR 418 to preserve fallback. Will run extra validation on next scheduled run.
Leah Park (security): Confirming org-policy change was intentional for folder 'experimental-onboard'; will delay rollout and add owner notifications.
Data Platform (via @dp-team): Confirmed ingestion backlog cleared; will run a targeted audit across other prod projects for missing 'env:deployment' tags.
